task_instance: Diagnose and fix Postgres egress anti-patterns (SELECT *, missing pagination, high-frequency static queries, app-side aggregation, JOIN duplication) for a sample e-commerce app (products/reviews/feature_flags schema) against a real local Postgres 16 instance with pg_stat_statements enabled, following the skill's 4-step workflow (diagnose/analyze/fix/verify).
evidence: Installed and started local PostgreSQL 16 (service postgresql start), enabled shared_preload_libraries='pg_stat_statements' in postgresql.conf and restarted, then `CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements` on a fresh `egressdemo` database. Built schema.sql (products with wide JSONB columns, reviews x50/product, feature_flags) and seed.py (200 products, 10000 reviews). Wrote app_before.py implementing the 5 anti-patterns named in the skill (SELECT * with no LIMIT, unbounded list endpoint, high-frequency feature-flag query with no caching, Python-side average-rating aggregation instead of SQL AVG, and a wide JOIN duplicating a large JSONB parent column across 50 child review rows). Ran simulated traffic, reset pg_stat_statements, then ran the skill's exact Step-1 diagnostic SQL (ORDER BY rows DESC / avg_rows_per_call DESC / calls DESC) which correctly surfaced: SELECT product_id, rating FROM reviews (20 calls, 200000 total rows -- the app-side aggregation query), SELECT * FROM products (30 calls, 6000 rows), SELECT * FROM feature_flags (500 calls -- caching candidate), and the JOIN query (10 calls, 500 rows incl. duplicated parent JSONB). Applied the Step-3 fixes in app_after.py (column pruning, LIMIT/OFFSET pagination, in-process cache for feature flags, SQL GROUP BY/AVG, splitting the JOIN into two column-limited queries). Reset stats again, re-ran equivalent traffic, and re-ran the diagnostics: total rows across all queries dropped from ~208,000 to ~6,000 (~97% reduction), feature_flags calls dropped from 500 real DB hits to 1 (cached), and the JOIN's duplicated wide-column transfer was eliminated by splitting into two targeted queries. This reproduces and verifies the skill's full diagnose->analyze->fix->verify loop end-to-end on a real Postgres instance with pg_stat_statements. (The neon.ts / `neon` CLI infra-as-code section of the skill was not exercised since it requires a paid Neon account, network access to neon.com, and API credentials -- out of scope for a local sandbox and not part of the skill's core deliverable, which is the query-level egress diagnosis and fix workflow.)
